thread:
Anna (sec): Heads up — I pushed a small RBAC tweak to the erasure-service role last night to remove `s3:ListBucket` for `service-account-erasure`. Canary ran in prod and I want a quick sanity check before we mark the change done. I'm worried about breaking the DSAR deletion proofing path.

Kevin (infra): Which envs did you change? staging or prod?

Anna (sec): Only prod; canary roll started ~02:10 UTC. I noticed one failed delete in prod around 02:47 that looked like a KMS permission denied during rewrap.

SRE-OnCall: I paged in at 02:50. Logs show: ```ERROR eraser: delete_failure user=svc-erasure@redwood key=projects/infra/locations/global/keyRING/key1 status=PERMISSION_DENIED``` Also the archived snapshot object is still present in cold storage for that DSAR id.

Maria (privacy): If a deletion fails we need to record it as a retention-exception / legal-hold note and produce an audit artifact showing the attempt + failure reason. Requestors will want a timeline.

Kevin (infra): Quick mitigation is to roll the RBAC change back on that service account in prod and re-run the delete job for the failed DSARs. Curious why removing ListBucket caused a KMS DENIED — could be the eraser workflow lists objects, reads metadata, then calls KMS.Rewrap; maybe we also tightened KMS permissions.

Anna (sec): IAM diff: I removed `s3:ListBucket` and tightened KMS perms with a conditional (time-based). That conditional might be too strict and caused intermittent failures.

SRE-OnCall: I can replay the job from the failed tombstone batch once access is restored. Before running anything, we should capture and stash the failed attempt evidence: stacktraces, auditlog ids, and KMS request ids so Privacy/Legal have proof. ops-bot, can you dump correlated audit entries?

ops-bot: auditbot: found 3 entries correlated to trace `00-abc123`: ```proto: { methodName: 'google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt', status: PERMISSION_DENIED, principal: 'serviceAccount:svc-erasure@redwood' }``` Also S3 API calls around the same trace: `GetObject` succeeded but `DeleteObject` returned 403 for same principal.

Anna (sec): OK — looks like two separate misconfigs: RBAC for S3 and a conditional on the KMS key. Proposed plan: 1) rollback RBAC change immediately, 2) tag affected DSARs in tracker with `delete-proof-needed`, 3) re-run deletion once perms restored, 4) produce a signed deletion receipt (include auditlog ids + kms request ids + snapshot digests) and hand to Privacy.

Maria (privacy): I agree. I'll open a retention-exception ticket and attach the artifacts. Legal wants explicit evidence that we attempted deletion and why it failed, plus the final completion time.

Kevin (infra): Two safety follow-ups: a) make eraser emit the KMS request id in structured logs (we currently have trace id but not the KMS rpc id), b) add a preflight check that verifies `kms:Decrypt` + `s3:DeleteObject` perms before running any erase batch.

Anna (sec): I can add a `--preflight-check` flag to the job that performs a dry-run permissions check against a small sample object and KMS key. I'll open a tiny PR and request an urgent deploy+revert path.

SRE-OnCall: Once rollback is live I'll trigger the re-run and post results. ETA ~30m after rollback.

Maria (privacy): For the two affected DSARs, can we add an explanatory note in the request timeline that we attempted deletion at 02:47 UTC and include when final deletion completed? Legal prefers that explicit audit-proof.

Kevin (infra): Also let's add a runbook item: any RBAC change touching erasure or KMS policies must have a Privacy reviewer and a preflight verification step. I can add the checklist item to `docs/rbac-runbook.md`.

Anna (sec): Added checklist to PR and will include the Privacy reviewer. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9876

ops-bot: :thumbsup: created retention-exception record REQ-2023-421 and will auto-attach audit bundle if delete job returns 403/PERMISSION_DENIED.

SRE-OnCall: Update: rollback completed at 03:25 UTC, re-run started at 03:28. First batch succeeded; second batch had a transient 503 but retried and succeeded. I'll upload the proof bundle once finished.

Maria (privacy): Thanks. Please include `kms_key_version`, `kms_request_ids`, and `audit_log_ids` in the proof bundle so Legal can verify end-to-end.

Anna (sec): Proof bundle uploaded: https://internal.redwood/proofs/eraser/1743218888-reqs.zip — contains structured logs, KMS request ids, S3 object digests, and replay commands.

SRE-OnCall: Verified both DSARs show `status=deleted` in the tracker. Closing loop — will follow up with a short postmortem and the RBAC runbook change.

Maria (privacy): Closing retention-exception after Legal sign-off. Thanks all.
